title: 2.3 OIL
summary: This chapter surveys the structure of the oil market, from how crude is discovered, classified, and traded globally to how it's refined into products that trade more regionally. It covers the mechanics of futures and physical contracts — naming conventions, pricing methods like CMA and Posting Plus, and the basic contract types — alongside the refining process itself, including distillation, cracking, and the crack spread that ties crude and product prices together. It also works through the major refined products (gasoline, diesel, heating oil, kerosene, and heavy fuel oil) and their grading and formulation, plus the biofuel side of the market — ethanol, biodiesel, RINs, and the corn crush spread. Throughout, it introduces the benchmark crudes and terminology used to describe quality, pricing, and market participants across this chain.
